newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks make new leaps on bluechip demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks make new leaps on bluechip demand.

text.p: Colombia stocks made new leaps Monday amid heavy demand for financial and manufacturing sector bluechips, brokers said.
Bogota's IBB index climbed 6.03 percent to hit 1,004.27, its highest level since Jan. 18, 1995, amid a 3.17 billion peso volume.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 5.12 percent to close at 15,258.88, its highest level since Sept. 7, 1995, amid a 4 billion peso volume.
"It was a frenetic session although towards the end of the day there was quite a lot of speculation, which may mean that we see some price correction in the next few days," said one Bogota broker.

In the year to date, the IBB has shown an 18 percent gain, compared with 11.8 percent in the whole of 1996. Demand in Bogota was fueled by pension funds, insurance companies and to a lesser extent foreign funds.
Despite the recent leaps, brokers said overall volumes of shares on offer was still very limited.
They said several factors are driving up stocks, including the perception that after little price variation in the last three years Colombian stocks are considered very cheap.

Moreover, new regulations, introduced on Jan. 1, mean fixed income investors have been saddled with a new tax of between 1 percent and 7 percent on earnings depending on the maturity of the paper, thereby prompting them to move into stocks.
In addition, changes in the way Colombian pension funds are obliged to calculate annual returns have also stimulated demand for stocks, brokers said.
"There may be a little price correction over the coming days but I would expect to see overall demand continuing. There's a lot of big investors looking to buy right now," said another Bogota trader.
